title: Algorithms
theory: Define what a result means before implementing the algorithm. Sorting must preserve all original values, including duplicates. Search must specify what happens when the target is absent.
Binary search depends on sorted data. Each step discards part of the remaining search interval. Your boundary updates must shrink that interval even for one element and missing targets.

Count comparisons on increasingly large inputs instead of relying only on elapsed time. Big-O describes growth, not a promise about exact seconds. Separate the cost of sorting from the cost of searching.
Recursion needs a base case and progress toward it. Trace a tiny input by hand. These labs assess output automatically; your chosen algorithm and complexity argument are reviewed through the rubric.

quiz.explanation: A missing target can require examining every element.
Sorting reorders elements; it does not remove or change them.

quiz.prompt: Why must recursive calls approach a base case?
quiz.explanation: Without progress, calls may continue until resources are exhausted.

quiz.prompt: You sort once, then make many searches. What costs should a comparison include?
quiz.explanation: Preprocessing is part of the total work.

quiz.prompt: For sorted [2,4,6], target 5 is missing. A correct search should?
quiz.explanation: Missing targets must also reduce the interval to an empty search range.
